label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
Dear Mr Kehinde Ogunleye,

Good day, sir. Thank you for picking up my bag and calling the number on my lab manual. I’m grateful that you kept it safe instead of throwing it away. I know many people might not have taken the trouble to contact me.

I’m the student who left the black Jansport bag on the Oshodi-to-Igando danfo on Friday evening, 6 November, when I came down at Ikotun. The bag contains my lab manual, dissecting kit, student ID card, two textbooks, calculator and glasses.

Sir, I understand that you may have spent time and money keeping the bag and reaching me, and I would like to thank you for your help. However, the ₦40,000 you asked for is more than I can afford. I’m a first-year student, and even the bag and books together are not worth that amount. I can manage **₦10,000** for your transport and as a thank-you, but that is all the allowance I have.

My BIO 101 practical is on Wednesday, 11 November, at 10 a.m., and I need my dissecting kit to be allowed into the lab. My ID card and glasses are also important to me. Please, I’m asking that you return my belongings to me; I cannot agree to pay ₦40,000 for them.

Kindly let me know a day and time **before Wednesday** when we can meet. Since you said you live around Ikotun, we could meet during the day at Ikotun roundabout or by the gate of Ikotun Police Division, whichever is more convenient. I’ll come with my roommate, Adaeze.

Thank you again, sir. Please reply and let me know when and where you can meet.

Kind regards.
